correctness.rationale: Exact table cylinder test guarantees the stopping property for every locally finite counting measure; a.s. Poisson simplicity and the occupied-selected count bound of two give the pathwise point bound. An attempted stopped CTDT must initially expose positive intensity from cell 2 or 3 on the empty configuration, but a positive-probability configuration avoiding the same initial history forces exclusion of that cell from its target. Continuity and observed-history stopping force a positive symmetric-difference measure, a contradiction. A standalone finite program passed; the analytic proof handles the continuum and all CTDTs.

value.rationale: A recent general theorem establishes attainability when a diffuse Poisson stopping set reveals at most one point; identifying two as sufficient for failure is a sharp structural transition, not a routine restatement of prior unbounded nonattainment. The counterexample remains compact, has finite diffuse intensity, and rules out the weaker stopped region-equality property with an explicit contradiction.
